steps.text: Welcome to the Minecraft Dungeons Walkthrough!

Minecraft Dungeons is a relatively easy completion which takes approximately 15-20 hours. The base game contains 24 achievements, worth a total of 1,000 Gamerscore, 5 of which are worth 100 each. Only one achievement requires co-operative play. The game does not yet support cross-platform play, although it may be added in a free future update.
There are two DLC packs - Jungle Awakens and Creeping Winter, each with 5 achievements worth 130 and 120 gamerscore respectively.

The game requires a minimum of three playthroughs (one on each difficulty) for a completion, though it is likely you will re-play missions regardless to find better loot. There are no missable achievements, because you can simply re-play a mission if you need to.

If you've played any dungeon crawler before, you will find Minecraft Dungeons to be fairly simplistic in comparison; but it is not without its unique mechanics and enjoyable gameplay. The controls are easy to pick up - the game will show you these in the tutorial.

You will earn the majority of the achievements through normal gameplay, but at the end of this walkthrough I will include a list of those you may not have unlocked, with some tips you can use to unlock them.
What does this walkthrough aim to do?
Provide hints and tips to maximise your playing experience
Provide information for mopping up achievements you may not have earned in your playthrough
Provide tips for grinding levels (for enchantment points) and emeralds (for power levels), and
Provide instructions for unlocking the 5 secret missions.

This game has procedural dungeon generation, so it is difficult to provide a 'do this, do that' walkthrough for completing missions, finding chests, etc. Therefore, this walkthrough consists more of information I wish I knew before playing, rather than a linear, step-by-step approach you'd find with a game that doesn't have procedural generation. I encourage you to explore every side-route before following your waypoint so that you'll find more chests and secrets.

sections.title: 2. Minecraft Dungeons General hints and tips

steps.text: LevelingExperience Points, including enchantingLevel XP FarmingPower LevelWindows 10 Soggy Cave Obsidian Chest Aim-Assist Glitch
Unable To Verify Game Ownership Error
A final comment, before you begin...
Teleport (to a friend in co-op): / F1, then F2, F3 or F4
You can remap all controls via the pause menu.
Note: Opening your map, or the pause menu doesn't pause the game! Make sure you are clear of enemies before pausing.
Defeating enemies and opening chests grant the chance of consumables dropping. Interact with these to pick them up.
Apple - Heals 20% of your maximum health over 3 seconds.
Bread - Heals 100% of your maximum health over 30 seconds.
Pork - Heals 50% of your maximum health over 10 seconds.
Melon (Jungle Awakens DLC missions) - Heals 75% health over 15 seconds.
Cooked Salmon (Creeping Winter DLC missions) - Heals 35% health over 8 seconds.

Shadow Brew - You become invisible until your next melee attack. Don't rely on these potions, because it's RNG-based whether or not they drop. However, they can help you sneak past large groups of enemies if you don't want to defeat them. Your first attack will deal 8x damage (and then the potion effect wears off).
Strength Potion - Deal double damage for 30 seconds. If you have Shadow Brew active too, 9x damage.
Swiftness Potion - Boosts movement speed for 20 seconds. Artefact speed buffs stack with this potion.
Oakwood Brew (Jungle Awakens DLC missions) - Grants immunity to poison for 15 seconds.
Sweet Brew (Creeping Winter DLC missions) - Grants immunity to frozen effects for 20 seconds.
Arrow Bundle - Adds ammo for your ranged weapon.

TNT - You can hold up to three of these at one time. Use your ranged attack to throw them and stay clear of the blast radius (it will show a white outline around the TNT when it lands). You cannot use your ranged weapon when holding TNT, you must throw the TNT first. TNT is useful against large groups of mobs, but ineffective against bosses and mini bosses.

When you die, you are saved by a Totem of Undying up to three times. The fourth time you die, it's game over and you must start the mission again. On Soggy Swamp, don't roll into the swamp, as you'll die, but the game is generous when it comes to falling out of the map. It won't spend a life but will take some health away from you. If you're on low health when you fall out of the map, it may take enough health away to drop you to 0 and therefore spend a life.
There Are Two Different Aspects of Leveling Your Character: Experience Points and Power Level:

Experience points are earned by defeating enemies. When you level up, you earn an enchantment point. You can use these points to enchant your weapons and give them special abilities, such as a chance to heal you and co-op allies within a certain radius, heal you for a percentage of a defeated mob's maximum health, increase the critical hit chance or damage, or cause the enemy to explode when they die, damaging other enemies around it. There are also enchantments which increase the likelihood of emeralds, consumables and/or loot dropping from defeated enemies.
Each enchantment has three levels of effectiveness. Common enchantments cost 1, 2, then 3 enchantment points, and Powerful enchantments cost 2, 3, then 4.

Everybody's play style is different, so I encourage you to experiment with these enchantments as you progress to see which is best suited for your play style. For example, I prefer Leeching over Radiance, and I rely heavily on Potion Barrier, which absorbs 90% of all damage for up to 9 seconds after using a health potion. (Leeching heals you for a percentage of a defeated enemies maximum health, whereas Radiance has a chance to heal you and allies close to you for 'X' amount each hit, so high-speed weapons are recommended here for maximum effectiveness).

As you progress through the game you'll find loot with more than one enchantment slot, up to a maximum of three. It all depends on the RNG for the loot drop. The achievement 'Maxed Out and Geared Up' requires your melee and ranged weapons and your armor to each have three enchantments at level 3, so the minimum character level required to achieve this is 54.
Equip a Gear set consisting of fully enchanted items (3 Enchantment Slots upgraded to Level 3).

It is not possible to remove enchantment points from your weapons/armor, so choose wisely; however, you can salvage the item for emeralds, which makes all the used enchantment points from that item available for use elsewhere. Doing this destroys the item.

Load up Redstone Mines on the hardest difficulty you can comfortably manage large groups of enemies on. Make your way through the mission until you find a mob spawner (the more the better) and set yourself up far enough away so you don't damage it when you attack, but close enough to defeat the spawning enemies as quickly as possible. If there are multiple spawners, place yourself between them. Sometimes enemies get stuck on the spawners, so having an artefact like the horn, which will push them back, or the fishing rod, to pull them in, could work well here. All you have to do is stand in one spot (on Windows 10, hold Shift) and attack the enemies as they get close. You'll earn a lot of XP and level up quickly, earning those all-important enchanting points.

Your power level is based on the level of your equipped items (melee, armor, ranged and three artefacts which provide specific buffs, abilities, or healing). You power level is the most important aspect of the game, as it determines the power level range for loot drops. When you select a mission to play, before selecting 'Start Mission' you will see up to six difficulties to play the mission on. Beneath this is a recommended power level and it will tell you the power level range for loot drops. The higher your power level, the higher that range will be. As of patch 1.4.3.0 - September 8, 2020, the maximum power level has been increased from 113 to 118.
Windows 10 Soggy Cave Obsidian Chest Aim-Assist Glitch

When you have unlocked the secret mission Soggy Cave, a player with a high power level can carry you through the beginning of the mission, and then can use an aim-assist glitch to skip the rest of the mission, fast-tracking you to an obsidian chest. At least one player is required to have an Xbox controller connected to do this. This is a questionable method, so use it at your own risk. I expect it to be patched, because it's not how the game was intended to be played. You can equip the loot and repeat the same method to boost your power level to about 80 in less than an hour. You can also do this solo, but it would require you clearing the enemies yourself, which would take longer if you're at a lower power level.

Run through the first part of the mission (outside) as quickly as possible, passing enemies if you can, until there is a bridge you must cross. You will probably have to defeat the enemies on the bridge. Enter the cave and run past the enemies in the first part of that room. Run North and you will see two doorways on the left, one of which you cannot access because it is blocked by a wall. Run into the West corner of that wall, click into the doorway with your mouse, then press and it should pull you through the doorway and to the obsidian chest. Leave the room North-West and make your way back to the boat you started at.
All secret missions will be covered in the 'Secret Missions' section of the walkthrough.

As of patch 1.4.3.0 - September 8, 2020, the Wandering Trader and Blacksmith have changed. The Mystery Merchant replaces the function of the Wandering Trader and Blacksmith, and the Blacksmith has been re-purposed for upgrading your equipment. If you completed the game on Apocalypse difficulty prior to the update, the traders will automatically be at your camp, but their upgrade slots won't retroactively unlock - you'll need to grind the requirements again to unlock more slots. If you started playing the game after the update, you'll need to find them in specific missions.

The Village Merchant arrives at camp after freeing him in Creeper Woods. He sells common and rare items and you can unlock more slots by freeing villagers (including pandas in Jungle Awakens) in missions.

The Blacksmith arrives at camp after freeing him in the Redstone Mines. You can give the blacksmith an item to reroll its power level. Prior to patch 1.4.3.0 - September 8, 2020, there was no way to remove enchantment points from your gear, but it is now possible by upgrading your items with the blacksmith. The available enchantments are not rerolled, only the power level and damage range of the item etc. When you give the item to the blacksmith you will get your enchantment points back and after completing three missions you can take the newly upgraded item back from him and re-apply your enchantment points. The level of the upgraded item is determined by the power level range of your last three missions, so if you're going for the highest range possible, run the hardest (and therefore highest power level range) mission three times for the best possible outcome.

The Gift Wrapper arrives at camp after freeing him in Soggy Swamp. You can use him to gift items to another player in your camp. The enchantment points on the item are refunded and the item is re-rolled to the recipients recommended power level. Traded items cannot be re-traded.

The Luxury Merchant arrives at camp after freeing him in Cacti Canyon. He sells items higher than your power level, but at a high price. If your power level is close to 113, some of the items he sells will be lower in power level - it seems to even out as you get towards the highest possible power levels. You can unlock more slots by defeating powerful mobs in missions.
The Mystery Merchant arrives at camp after freeing him in Pumpkin Pastures. He sells loot crates for various items and you can unlock more slots by defeating enchanted enemies.
Perhaps the best piece of advice I can give you in this:

Do not spam-buy crates, hoping for a unique power level 113 item! The item you received is based on your power level. Once you have a few thousand emeralds, go into your inventory and equip any weapons, armor and artefacts with the highest power level. Make a single trade, and if the item you receive is a higher power level than what you have equipped, equip the new item and repeat. You will quickly rise in power levels with this method, which is vital for making it through to the end of the game. You can then salvage unwanted items for a return in emeralds. The achievement 'Oooh! Shiny!' requires you to collect 5000 emeralds total, not to have 5000 emeralds, so you can spend them whenever you want.
When selecting a crate to buy, you can also see the power level range of the item you will receive.

I often see people saying the only way to play is to equip and play with the highest power level, but with this method I do not think is necessary. It can certainly help with speedrunning the game, but if you have a piece of armor with a bonus or enchantment you like, but it is a few power levels below everything else, I would recommend keeping that item until you find a replacement you are happy with, or can upgrade it at the Blacksmith. On several occasions I found a new piece of armor I thought I would like, so I equipped it and salvaged the old piece only to find it wasn't suitable for my play style, or the enchantments weren't as useful. You'll make these mistakes in your playthrough, but the best way to learn is to make the mistakes for yourself. At least with this information you can be aware of them.

With that said, on my co-op playthrough I played with a rule of if I looted an item with a higher power level than what I had equipped, I equipped it regardless of the abilities or enchantments. My partner and I didn't have too much trouble, but we did have to adjust our play style a little.
Some enemies have unique abilities, which can prove challenging if you don't know how to counter them.

It's generally a good idea to target Enchanters first, as they buff nearby enemies. If you can't get to them, try to walk the buffed enemies away from the Enchanter (they don't tend to move around a lot), and they'll go out of range and lose their buff. Next in your list of priorities should be:

Geomancers - They summon stone columns to prevent you from moving (usually between you and them), and exploding columns that do a lot of damage. Exploding columns will flash red, which is an easy way to differentiate the two. Geomancers also have a long line of sight. There are usually a few of them together on higher difficulties.

Summoners - They summon a lot of enemies (mainly Wraiths and Zombies) between you and them. Try to take out the summoner first, otherwise you can quickly get overrun. Once you defeat the Summoner you can defeat the enemies it summoned.
Wraiths - They will teleport around you when they take damage, but also summon a square of blue flames around you which does a lot of damage.

Armored ranged mobs (Skeletons and Pillagers) - These are ranged mobs that do a lot of damage. You can be quickly overwhelmed by them. Spiders will shoot webs at you, preventing you from moving for a short period of time.

Other enemies are easier to defeat. For example, Pillagers are fast, but weak. Husks have high HP, but are slow. If there are Creepers, try to trigger them and roll away just before they explode so that they will damage nearby enemies. If you're able to, try to defeat a small group of Creepers with your melee weapon before they explode. If not, consider swapping your weapon out for one that does more damage, or use area of effect enchantments, such as Lightning or Swirling.
When you encounter a mini-boss you'll see their HP at the top of the screen when you're close to them. They have a lot of HP, but are easy to defeat when you exploit their weaknesses.
Endermans - They frequently teleport around you and do a moderate amount of damage. I found using weapons with fast attacks caused it to flinch a lot and not be able to do too much damage.

Evokers - They summon a chain of bear traps in front of them which do a lot of damage. When you notice them raise their hands, dodge to the side of them and continue your attack and you should dodge the traps.

Redstone Golems - Their movement is slow, but because they are so large, they can be difficult to manoeuvre around in small spaces. I found running away and firing shots with a high-powered crossbow helped, but allowing them to get close to you so they hit the floor to spit out the lava mines is also effective, as you can swoop in to attack. Using the enchantment Potion Barrier (-90% damage for up to 9 seconds after using a healing potion) alongside a fast weapon and Death Cap Mushroom artefacts is a good way to do a considerable amount of damage to any enemy mobs, whilst taking minimal damage in the process.

The Four Horsemen - They will randomly spawn when you don't expect them to, but are fairly easy to defeat. Go for one at a time and you shouldn't have any trouble with them. They can spawn in Cacti Canyon on Default difficulty, and Creeper Woods, Soggy Swamp, Pumpkin Pastures, Cacti Canyon, Redstone Mine and Desert Temple on Adventure difficulty and above. They can also spawn in Fiery Forge in Apocalypse difficulty.
Main mission bosses will be covered in the 'Story' section of the walkthrough.

A lot of people have reported that the Hero DLC (cape and chicken) are not accessible to them. From what I've seen, the developers are blaming it on the Windows 10 May update not being released yet. I have also seen people say even after updating Windows, they still cannot access the DLC. I do not have the Windows update yet but was able to fix it using this method by chance, so I do not know if this will 100% fix it for you.

Go to the main menu and into character selection. Copy your character and delete the new duplicate. Careful! When you copy your character, items and emeralds aren't carried over, so make sure you delete the new character. You can see how many emeralds they have from the character select screen. This seemed to fix the problem for me, and when I loaded up my character I was able to select the coat hanger in my inventory to equip the chicken and cloak.
If you're on Xbox One, remember you need to download the DLC after purchasing it. Go to the game info page and look at the DLC. If you own the DLC, you should be able to click 'Install'.
Unable to Verify Game Ownership Error

If you encounter this error when launching the game, do not reinstall the game. There are currently no cloud saves and Microsoft makes it very difficult to back up your save. Reinstalling the game will mean you will have to start from the beginning again.

Each time this has happened to me, I restarted my PC and had no problems going forward. Hopefully it will work for you. It's apparently related to Game Pass, but can still happen even if you own the game.

You can join a friend's game and if they are a high power level, they can carry you through the game. Loot everything you can, as it drops on a per-player basis and is not shared. Equip the highest power level items to constantly increase your power level. If a friend is grinding you through the power levels, especially with the Soggy Cave glitch on Windows 10, it should take less than an hour to get to power level 80+. Then, farming XP in the Redstone Mines mission can get your player level up (see below). There are several achievements which require you to open 'X' number of chests, defeat 'X' amount of enemies and/or specific enemies. For these achievements, the enemies your friends defeat do not count towards your completion.

If you are both the same level, always equip a higher power level item when you receive it. You should be able to play through on the highest difficulty possible without much trouble, using the recommended/lowest difficulty for the last mission. In my co-op playthrough with a friend who had not played the game before, we only failed the final mission on the highest difficulty in Default mode but found it easier on the lowest difficulty after. Loot drops were not great, so you may find some grinding is required.

The level Creepy Crypt is perfect for farming emeralds, as there are a high number of enemies and chests. Check all of your looted weapons for the Prospector enchantment and keep the highest power level/damaging weapon you have that has this enchantment. You'll want to max the Prospector enchantment to level 3 so that more emeralds will drop from defeated enemies. If you have two Prospector enchantments available on a single weapon, great, they stack. Three? Fantastic, even more emeralds! If you find a Diamond Pickaxe, it has a buff which has the same effect as Prospector but is not an enchantment. From testing, it seems to act the same as a single Level 3 Prospector, and definitely is not as good as a double Prospector weapon, so keep this in mind. Did you find a power level 113 triple Prospector Diamond Pickaxe? Go buy a lottery ticket and don't forget my commission when you win!
It's also possible to find some unique Sickles called The Last Laugh, which cause mobs to drop more emeralds.

I've noticed this difference: The Diamond Pickaxe says, 'Finds More Emeralds', whereas The Last Laugh says, 'Mobs Drop More Emeralds'. In testing, I've been unable to find a difference. I thought at first the Diamond Pickaxe would find more emeralds from vases and chests, but I didn't notice much of a difference, and when defeating mobs it animates an emerald when the ability triggers, leading me to believe they have the same effect of causing mobs to drop more emeralds.

Don't forget, you can also salvage loot you don't want to use. This will make up a large portion of your haul after running Creepy Crypt. Just open your inventory, select the item, and select 'Salvage'. Immediately after salvaging an item you can undo the action, otherwise as soon as you click away it's gone for good. Be careful.
If you explore the campgrounds, you can find Lobby Chests, which contain 50 emeralds. This isn't an efficient method for farming emeralds, as there's a lot of running involved.
When in a mission, press / Tab and the map will be shown as an overlay as you're playing. This saves you constantly going in and out of the full map view.

You will see artefacts and weapons referring to Souls in their description - more commonly 'Requires Souls'. If you have an artefact or weapon with an ability that requires souls, you will automatically collect them as you defeat enemies. You'll see the white soul floating out of the defeated enemy towards you, just as XP orbs do, but slower. Beneath your artefacts you'll see the soul bar - when it's full you can't collect any more.

Some artefacts, such as the Corrupted Beacon consume and convert your collected souls into devastating damage. This is a viable tactic for defeating bosses quickly. Other artifacts, such as the Soul Healer will convert collected souls into healing for you and the most injured nearby ally (including Wolves, Llamas and Golems).
I encourage you to experiment with a soul setup. Getting the right combination of soul enchantments, artefacts and weapons can help considerably.
Behind the Nether Portal at the far East side of camp, climb the hill behind the tree.
Go into the small cave and climb the hill. Roll across the gap and climb to the top and an Obsidian chest will spawn.
You can only claim this chest once per character, so you may want to hold off until you are a high power level to maximise its potential.
A final comment, before you begin...

Don't try to rush missions. Explore as much of each mission as possible before you follow your waypoint. Do this and you'll find more secrets and chests and defeat more enemies with the chance to drop loot. When you see emerald jars, interact with them and collect the emeralds.

Some areas require you to roll across a gap to get to them, but these usually reward you with an Obsidian chest, which drops great loot. Don't forget to mouse-over suspicious looking switches and non-enemy skeletons if their outline changes to white. These are secrets, and they usually trigger a raid with a loot chest once you have defeated the enemies. Some chests aren't visible until you get near them, and they'll spin up and out of the ground.
You do not have to follow a specific order, but I have listed the missions in the order it gives them to you when you select 'view next' from the map at the campsite.

Due to large parts of missions being procedurally generated, it is difficult to provide a 'do this, do that' walkthrough for completing missions, finding chests, etc. Therefore, this walkthrough consists more of information I wish I knew before playing, rather than a linear, step-by-step approach you'd find with a game that doesn't have procedural generation. I encourage you to explore every side-route before following your waypoint so that you'll find more chests and secrets.

The tactics I used to defeat bosses mainly consisted of shooting at them with a high-powered crossbow from range. During my playthrough I didn't experiment much with Souls, but with the right setup you can produce devastating DPS against large groups of enemies and bosses.
This is the tutorial mission. Pay attention to the prompts, which teach you the controls and game mechanics.
As soon as you start, head South-East and roll across the gap over the water. Follow this small island to a golden chest.
Loot the chest and you will unlock 'Fancy That!'.
Find and open your first 'fancy' treasure chest.

After picking up some arrows and defeating a skeleton on a platform, head East. You may be able to enter the lighthouse, which may have an Obsidian chest in. In testing, I believe this only spawns when you are re-playing the mission after beating the Arch-Illager, but it could be I had bad RNG rolls.
When the objective 'Secure the inner gate' appears, loop up and around the stone wall toward the house to unlock a secret chest.
Head down the steps and under the trees to your left to find a gap in the fence. Another secret chest is next to this house.
After completing the mission you will unlock 'Happy Camper'.
Complete Squid Coast and set up camp.

As the name suggests, there are a lot of Creepers in this mission. Remember you can roll away after triggering them, and they will explode and damage other mobs around them, or you can use your bow if your melee attacks aren't strong enough. There are also a fair number of Skeleton Archers, but they are mostly spread out, so you shouldn't get overwhelmed. Don't forget to defeat passive mobs as you go - there's about 20 or so in this mission. When you complete the mission, you will unlock 'Out of the woods'.
By now you should also have unlocked or be well on your way to 'Wooden Sword'.

You may encounter some Geomancers in this mission. They have a long line of sight and summon stone columns to block your path. Some of the columns will glow red and explode, dealing a lot of damage. Try to focus your damage on the Geomancers first, or else you may get overrun.

After you cross the large castle wall, the Arch-Illager will block your path and trigger a raid. Enemies will spawn in to attack you. After defeating each wave, the gate will unlock leading you to the drawbridge. More enemies will spawn in as you flip the switches to lower the drawbridge.

You'll start to encounter armored enemies now. They have more health and tend to do more damage, so try to focus on them first. You should also encounter your first pig chest - defeat it to have it drop the golden chest on its back for you to loot!

At the end of the mission you will ring the warning bell and a raid will trigger. You'll also encounter Enchanters here if you haven't already. They enchant nearby enemies to buff them in different ways. Try to defeat the Enchanters first, as they are quite powerful.

When you defeat the last wave of the raid, an Evoker will spawn. Evokers summon a chain of bear traps in front of them which do a considerable amount of damage. If you are using melee to defeat the Evoker, when they raise their hands dodge to the side to avoid the traps. Alternatively, keep your range and use your bow. After defeating the Evoker, a gate will unlock for you to complete the mission.
Don't roll/fall into the swamp on this mission, as you will die. There are a couple of hidden chests on small islands you can roll to.

You'll encounter Baby Zombies, which move very fast but are easy to defeat. You'll also encounter Slimes, which spawn multiple smaller Slimes when defeated, which then spawn even more smaller Slimes when defeated. You'll also encounter Witches, who throw poison potions at you. Stay out of the pink/purple gas cloud as these do a fair amount of damage over time.
When you have the 'Destroy the brews' task, don't forget to collect the emeralds that drop when you destroy each brew!

When you enter the cave you may encounter an Enderman. They will teleport around you to try and damage you from behind, but are fairly easy to defeat. They flinch often, so melee seems to be the best option here.
A little bit after the cave you'll enter a large stone area. If you have your map overlay open, you should see a chest. It can be easy to miss, depending on how the mission has spawned.

At the end of the mission you will encounter your first boss, the Corrupted Cauldron. It spawns pink/purple fire around its base, which does a lot of damage, so a ranged attack is the best option here. It will also spit out purple Slimes, so be sure to defeat those that land near you. As you enter the area you will see a wooden fence on the top of the hill. You may be able to stand here and use your bow to defeat the Cauldron without it being able to hit you, though the fences usually block your arrows.
When you complete the mission, you will unlock 'The Plot Thickens'.
Complete Pumpkin Pastures and Soggy Swamp.
By now you should also have unlocked or be well on your way to 'Worked like a Charm', 'Cha-ching!', and 'Scrappy Scout'.
Enchant an item and upgrade the enchantment to Tier 3.

This is the only mission where you will encounter mob spawners. They have a lot of HP and constantly spawn mobs around you. Go in when there's no cooldown on your health potion to defeat the mob spawner as quickly as possible, or you could decide to try and run past it. Watch out for minecarts on the tracks - they do a lot of damage if they hit you!
You'll also encounter armored Pillagers with crossbows. They do a lot of damage, so try to focus them before other slower enemies. If you can, save your arrows for the boss.

At the end of the mission you will encounter a Redstone Golem boss. They are large, difficult to dodge, and move reasonably fast. Let it get close to you and it will hit the ground and spawn lava mines. You can attack it when it's immobile. If a lava mine spawns on you, roll away from it, as they do a lot of damage. You may also want to consider running in a circle around the area, taking shots with your bow to defeat him. Either method works well.
After you defeat the Redstone Golem a gate will open. There are a few enemies on the other side, so don't rush to the end to complete the mission if you're low on health.

There are a lot of archer enemies on this mission with Geomancers and Enchanters and you can quickly be overrun by them. Go in hard and fast with your melee to clear groups or pick them off at range. If you're lucky, you'll also encounter some Redstone Golems in confined spaces.

When you get to mission objective 'Overload the cores' you need to activate cores, which will explode. Stay clear of the trenches, as the fire deals a lot of damage. This area has the potential to spawn several secret chests and areas with chests which appear after you trigger a raid. Explore it well.

At the end of the mission you will encounter the Redstone Monstrosity boss. It behaves similarly to a Redstone Golem, but will spit lava mines out and will spawn magma cubes which roll around and damage you. There are four cores in this area, which you can trigger to overload and send the explosion down the channels. Try to manoeuvre the Redstone Monstrosity into the channels so it gets hit by the explosion, and do melee or ranged damage to it whenever possible.
After defeating the Redstone Monstrosity, heal up and let your cooldowns end. There are some enemies to clear on the pathway to the end of the mission.

This mission introduces a new game mechanic. You will be required to find a key and take it to a gate in order to progress. When you find it, melee the key to pick it up. If you take damage you may drop it and it may run away, or an enemy may take it, so keep an eye on it! Keys and gates are color coordinated - blue keys open blue gates, golden keys open gold gates - but it's very simple as it's always a mission objective and never a secret.

This mission also introduces you to new mobs. Husks are slow-moving heavy hitters, and take a lot of damage to defeat. Skeleton Horsemen may randomly appear - they don't do too much damage but focus on one at a time to defeat them.
There are large groups of enemies in this mission, but it's fairly open, so you should be able to separate small groups to pick them off from the main packs.
When you complete the mission, you will unlock 'Built on Sand, Set in Stone'.
Built On Sand, Set in Stone
Complete Redstone Mines and Cacti Canyon.
By now you should have unlocked or be well on your way to 'Break the Spell', 'Diamond Sword', 'Blast Radius' and 'Passive Aggressive''.
Kill any 10 mobs at once with TNT.

Desert temple introduces you to Summoners and Skeleton Vanguards. Summoners will summon large groups of enemies, so focus fire on them to defeat them as quickly as possible. Skeleton Vanguards have high defence, but once you've broken their shields, you should defeat them without trouble.

You will also encounter booby traps which deal a lot of damage if you get hit by them. Almost all of them are activated, and remain activated, when you walk over a switch. If you have a pet Wolf/Llama/Golem, expect them to die to the traps a lot - it gets quite frustrating.

Just after you unlock the door with the key, look for another door to your left which leads to a room where you can access a golden chest a secret level scroll after flipping three switches. (As of patch 1.3.2.0 - July 1, 2020 the golden chest is replaced by the secret level scroll. The method of farming the obsidian chest is still viable, however).
The room will usually be orientated in one way, but it is still possible to roll to a ledge and walk up to a golden chest.
If the room spawns in a different orientation, you can access an obsidian chest when you roll down to the ledge.
Speedrunning your way to these chests is a viable method to achieve good loot drops.
When you continue, you'll be raided by the Arch-Illager. Trigger the two blade traps in this area - they will come in handy to defeat the raid.

The boss in this mission is The Nameless One. He is fairly challenging to defeat, but as you have a large area for the battle, you can pull range to heal up. The boss will shoot green pulses at you, which do a lot of damage. Do your best to avoid them, using the stone columns if you need to. Shortly after this, they will spawn Skeleton Vanguards or duplicate and send seeking green pulses at you. Dodge these the best you can and then go in for the attack before repeating the process. A ranged attack against the boss and melee against the Skeleton Vanguards was how I dealt with this part of the mission.

After defeating the Nameless One, don't rush through the next area, as there are a lot of enemies including Wraiths, and possibly an Enderman. Make sure you recover from the boss fight before heading down the path.

This mission has a lot of heavily-armored Pillagers who do a lot of damage. There are also a lot of crossbow pillagers who can quickly overwhelm you when they're in groups. Try to pick them off one at a time without taking aggro from too many enemies at once.

When you leave the castle and enter the courtyard, look to the East. There is a well you can go into to enter the main castle through the back door. In the sewers there should be a pig chest and an Enderman or Evoker. Alternatively, you can find the key to unlock the front door. I suggest defeating every enemy in this area. There are a lot of them, so it should give you enough XP to level up.

After you get the objective 'Reach the throne room', you'll encounter an obsidian chest on a lowered platform. You can roll down to the chest to loot it and interact with the button in front of it to raise stairs. This will trigger a raid with a lot of archers. The stairs will also begin to raise slowly, so be ready to defend yourself from range or have a defence artefact ready.

At the end of the mission, if you're not using maximum speed buffs, don't try to run past the Arch-Illager to the door (you can get past before it closes if you're quick enough). You will get blocked in and will have to restart the mission. You must defeat the raid to trigger the door to open, and then the door to the end of the mission will work.
When you complete the mission, you will unlock 'High and Dry'.
Complete Desert Temple, Fiery Forge and Highblock Halls.

The final mission is by far the hardest in the game. There are a lot of armored crossbow Pillagers, and the Arch-Illager boss fight is definitely the hardest. I was able to defeat the Arch-Illager on Apocalypse difficulty, solo, at power level 75, using: an Exploding Crossbow, Totem of Regeneration, Deathcap Mushrooms, and Potion Barrier. I used all three of my lives in the boss fight. Towards the end I did my best to keep distance from the boss, using my ranged attack to chip away at the their health.

The final mission can take a while if you explore every route. You have to use piston jumps to get to areas, which usually have a lot of enemies on them, so go in prepared for a fight after each jump. Use the piston-pads to your advantage. Most have a 'return pad' that takes you back to the area you came from. Enemies can also use the pads, but you tend to lose aggro when you use them, so they usually don't follow you.

There are several opportunities to encounter Redstone Golems and a couple of areas containing a lot of enemies and Enchanters, which can be challenging, so try to pick off the Enchanters first. The first of these areas is usually found after heading through the halls and heading outside onto the wall again.

The Arch-Illager is defeated in two stages. The first stage is fairly easy and doesn't require a lot of damage. He will shoot purple cubes at you, which you must dodge. When you get close, he will teleport elsewhere, but try to save your arrows for the next bit.

In the second stage you have to defeat the Heart of Ender, which moves quickly around, leaving Ender fire in its path. It will spawn purple beams, which rotate clockwise. You need to run with these as close to the Heart of Ender as possible to avoid them. When they stop rotating, enemies will randomly spawn from the ground and shoot lasers in the direction they are facing. Do your best to avoid these too.

During all of this, try to get ranged shots off at the Heart of Ender. If you're on Windows 10, don't aim for the head. Instead, mouse-over the Arch-Illager, who is at floor-level. and your ranged shots should hit.

You may also be able to exploit the boss's view distance in this area. If he teleports to the North-East corner, try to get to the North-West corner. In my playthrough the boss lost sight of me and stopped triggering its beam attacks. I shot it with an Accelerate/Infinity combo Exploding Crossbow and took him down quickly on Apocalypse difficulty.
Congratulations on completing Default difficulty. Now onto Adventure and then Apocalypse!
Defeat the Arch-Illager at the Obsidian Pinnacle.

With the exception of 'Life of the Party' (revive a downed friend 20 times), 'High Treason' was the last achievement I unlocked. By the time you reach Obsidian Pinnacle on Apocalypse difficulty, you'll have a good understanding of the game's mechanics and how to defeat the boss.
Defeat the Arch-Illager on Apocalypse difficulty.
If you still have achievements left to unlock, see the next section of the walkthrough for a list of achievements that may need grinding and how to unlock them.
Now that you have completed the game on Apocalypse difficulty, you should have most of the game's achievements. If not, I have listed them here with tips on how to quickly finish them.

Load up the mission Redstone Mines on the hardest difficulty you are comfortable with. When you find a room with a spawner, it will likely have several of them. Stick to one spot between the spawners and don't destroy them. You can farm levels and mobs by just defeating everything that spawns.
Load up the mission Squid Coast and immediately head South-East. Roll across the gap and follow the island. You'll find a gold-plated chest - open it.
Find and open your first 'fancy' treasure chest.

The secret mission Creepy Crypt contains a lot of chests to find, and a lot of enemies clustered into small rooms. You can farm about 2000 emeralds and 15-20 chests in 45 minutes on this mission. When TNT drops, pick it up and wait until you find a room with a lot of enemies huddled together - it should be easy to hit them with the TNT here.

Om Nom Nom (Eat 200 food items) is bugged, or rather, the way it is tracked is bugged. It only counts 20 at a time, so you must eat 20 or more food items and complete the mission for it to count 20. Pumpkin Pastures is a good mission for food drops, so play through that mission and you should easily have 20 food drops. Theoretically this should take less than 10 runs of 20.

As of game update 1.2.0.0 - June 17, 2020, the food dropped from tables in Highblock Halls counts towards this achievement, so you may decide to run through that mission for the better loot opportunities instead.

If you're still struggling with the TNT achievement, load up the secret mission ???, where there are a lot of enemies in small spaces. Once you have some TNT (randomly dropped by defeated enemies), try to cluster enemies into a large group and throw the TNT at them.
Kill any 10 mobs at once with TNT.

Load up the mission Redstone Mines with a friend or a second controller. Have the other player stand on the minecart tracks right at the beginning of the mission, and have them get downed by the minecart. Wait for the game to say on the right-hand side of the screen that the player needs revived, then revive them. Repeat 19 more times.

On Apocalypse difficulty you will pick up weapons and armor with three enchantment slots. You must enchant all three slots to level three on your Armor, Melee and Ranged weapons. If you only use Common enchantments, the minimum player level required to have enough enchantment points is 54.
Enchant an item and upgrade the enchantment to Tier 3.
Equip a gear set consisting of fully enchanted items (3 enchantment slots upgraded to level 3).

The artefact 'Tasty Bone' summons the wolf, and 'Wonderful Wheat' summons the Llama. These artefacts are dropped on any difficulty. 'Golem Kit', which summons the Iron Golem, starts dropping in Apocalypse difficulty. You do not have to have all three summoned at the same time, you just need to summon them at least once each throughout your gameplay.

To see if an item drops in a mission, select the mission from the map at the camp and above 'Start Mission' it will detail the gear and artefact drops in that mission. It is also possible to get them randomly from the Wondering Trader at camp.
Tasty Bone: Creeper Woods and Creepy Crypt.
Wonderful Wheat: Arch Haven, Cacti Canyon and Obsidian Pinnacle.
Use artefacts to summon the Wolf, Llama and Iron Golem allies at least once each.

Defeat Sheep, Pigs and Cows when you see them. (They also have a chance to drop consumables). Creeper Woods seems to be the mission with the highest number of passive mobs, so run through that mission a few times to finish this achievement.

Defeat enemies who are being enchanted by an Enchanter. You'll know they are enchanted because a purple beam will be flowing from the enchanter to the enemy you need to defeat. In apocalypse difficulty there will also be the chance for enemies to have enchantments, even if the Enchanter isn't present.

For efficiency, equip speed artifacts and/or armor and play on the lowest difficulty. When you interact with the 'New Location' scroll and unlock the secret mission, you can leave back to the menu/camp without finishing the mission if you want to.

Usually found after rescuing the first villager. Head down the path to the West and you'll find a stone structure with a glowing red block. Press the button and the door will open. Go through the door and in front of you will be a stone plinth with a scroll on it titled 'New Location'. Click on it.

This is heavily reliant on RNG. You will need to load into the mission, leave to the camp and re-load the mission until you get a favorable roll. Some people have reported this to take hours. For me it took about 20 minutes. Good luck!

Load the Soggy Swamp mission and immediately open your map. If you see 'Secrets 0/0', reload the mission until it shows as 'Secrets 0/1'. If you have completed the game on default difficulty and found the secret rune, it will be 0/2, not 0/1. You're looking for 'Secrets' to show as 0/1 pre-rune, or 0/2 post-rune. When you have this, continue through the mission, through the cave (after destroying the brews) and out the other side. The entrance will spawn as a side route away from the way-pointed route, like it did with Creepy Crypt. When you enter the cave you will need to activate a switch to trigger a raid and a bridge. At the end of the bridge is the scroll; between two flames.

Also reliant on RNG. This always spawns as a boat with a door you can enter on the main deck. (Other boats have a wooden portcullis style wall blocking the entrance). If you make it as far as needing to flip two switches to lower the drawbridge, restart the mission. It's possible for the boat to spawn past this point, but easier to restart and check the beginning of the mission again. Unlike Soggy Cave, this has no effect on the 'Secrets' count on your map view.

Load up Pumpkin Pastures and check each side route as you progress through the main route. You're looking for a wooden ship - the outline of which you can also see on your map. Enter the ship and claim the scroll. The first image below is a successful find. The second image is an example of a regular ship without the door, so you can easily tell the difference.
Load up the Highblock Halls mission. In the very first area you head down some stairs either side of two shields on the wall. Interact with one of the shields and the door will open between them.
Load up Desert Temple and progress through the mission until you have to unlock a gate with a gold key. After unlocking the gate, turn left at the crossroads above water.
In the next room you will have to check the four corners of the room and activate three switches (one in each corner and one corner will not have one).
Once all three switches have been activated, a platform to the scroll will be raised.
(Prior to game version 1.3.2.0 - July 1, 2020 there was a gold chest in the scroll location).

Load up Dingy Jungle and progress through the mission until you have the objective 'Cross the Canyon'. Do not follow your waypoint, instead head down the side alleys and you should find a doorway. If you get the objective 'Survive the Gauntlet', you have gone too far and need to turn back and explore the side alleys. The location of this door will be different, depending on how your mission has been generated.
Go through the doorway, which leads to an area with lava in the North-West.

In this area you will be raided by creepers. After defeating the enemies, look for a switch in the West, North-West and North-East part of the lava area. Activate each switch and bamboo gates will open in the South-West part of the lava area, leading to the scroll.
Loud up Frosted Fjord and progress through the mission until you have three buttons to press. Press the buttons and enter the door which opens.

In this cave, look for an area with stone pillars making the corners of a square, and a statue in the middle. The path will split off into two directions. Take the path your mission waypoint is not leading you down.

Note: This is another secret mission based on RNG. It does not count as a secret on your map view, so you will need multiple run-throughs to this point in the mission to see if the RNG roll was in your favor.
You'll arrive in a room with a waterfall and opening - take the opening.
You'll see another door above you - don't go there yet. Run through this area and you'll see a purple gate blocking your way. Run behind the gate and activate the wooden water wheel.
The gate you just passed will now be open, head through it and around the area to a stone platform. Stand on the platform to activate the switch to drop the next purple gate.
Use the bounce pads to reach the blue button on the wall.
When you press the button, the water level will drop. Drop down to the floor and enter the pirate ship's door to find the scroll.

You need to collect ten secret runes. When you are in the secret rune rooms (a purple area with the stone platforms), interact with the buttons in the square. Wait for the rune to appear, then interact with the rune. You can then leave back to the menu/camp without finishing the mission if you want to.

Once you have beaten the game on Default difficulty, there will be some bouncing pistons to get across to the other side of the church. From the map, head clockwise past the house with the pigs. You should see the pistons. Use them to clear the gap and continue clockwise around the centre hill. You'll find a small path under the trees which brings you round to the entrance of the church. Flip the switch to lower the bridge and you won't have to take this route every time from now on. Enter the church and head to the end of the room. Interact with the button on the wall and the first rune will light up. You can now find each secret rune on the other missions.

Head through the mission until you are tasked with rescuing 5 villagers. In the South-West corner of this area is a stone platform you can stand in. When you do, the platform will lower and trigger the door to appear below you. If you can't access the door, the switch is just above you next to a cluster of stones. The switch will cause the large stone platform surrounding the door to open up.

Head through the mission until you reach a large fortified wall with waterfalls coming out of it. You should be able to get onto the top of the wall via the destroyed section. Head all the way to the end of the wall and the button to unlock the door is behind some boxes.
At the end of the mission, after defeating the Corrupted Cauldron, look to the right of the door to exit the mission. The switch will be hidden behind some mushrooms next to a tall stone structure.

Head through the mission until you are tasked with rescuing the villagers for a second time. In the South-West/West part of this area you will find the switch behind the glowing redstone. It's a little tricky to spot, so (if you're on Windows 10) slowly mouse-over the areas until you see the white outline.
At the beginning of the mission when you first enter the cave you'll see a dead Redstone Golem. The switch is on the wall behind it.

Head through the mission until you reach the blue key. A gate will block your path and the Arch-Illager will raid you. After defeating the enemies, the gate will open. To the immediate South-West of this gate is a palm tree. The palm tree is between a small area of water and the gate. Behind this tree is the switch, which opens the door immediately behind the blue key.
Head through the mission until you need to find a gold key to open a locked gate. In the room immediately North-West of the gold key, there is a switch in the North corner behind a palm tree.

Head through the mission until you enter a large courtyard where you can either unlock the door with the key or head through the well and sewers to get into the castle. Hug the East wall of the castle and you'll find an unlit torch to interact with and open the door.

Head through the mission until you go indoors. Before leaving this indoor area there is a large library section with bookshelves. At the end of this section you can interact with one of the books to open the secret bookshelf door to the last rune.
Once all the runes are collected, go to the Camp and head back to the church. Interact with the button again. Head through the door and interact with the map to unlock the last mission, ???.
Jungle Awakens was released on September 8, 2020, alongside the Creeping Winter DLC. There are five achievements worth 130 Gamerscore.

Choose 'Dingy Jungle', the first mission in the Island Realms. Set the difficulty to Default and the difficulty slider to the lowest. Speed run the mission without dying or using your health potion to earn 'Survival Skills'. You shouldn't have much trouble on the lowest difficulty, but you can pick up health potions or use artefacts to heal.
Complete Dingy Jungle without using a healing potion or losing a life.

Then onto for 'Overgrown Temple', on Adventure or Apocalypse difficulty. If you're having trouble on Adventure difficulty, this is a sign you need to revisit some previous missions to increase your power level before returning to this mission.
Complete Overgrown Temple on Adventure or Apocalypse difficulty.
For 'Pandamonium', see Secret Missions for details on how to unlock the Panda Plateau secret mission. You can run through this mission and achieve the next achievement in the list in one sitting.
Complete the Panda Plateau secret mission.
The next two achievements require specific gear.

Ocelot Armor drops during Jungle missions. When it does, equip it at your camp and run through a Jungle mission on the lowest difficulty, making sure not to defeat any Ocelots. Don't use any explosive or area of effect weapons, and it might be worth trying to find a weapon with the smallest Area trait possible, to minimise the risk of hitting any Ocelots. You shouldn't have much trouble switching your gear out if they have these abilities, as you're on the lowest difficulty. You should also be able to run past most enemies on the lowest difficulty.
If the Ocelot Armor is a low power level and you're struggling on the lowest difficulty setting, don't forget you can upgrade the Armor at the Blacksmith.
Wear the Ocelot Armour and complete any mission featuring Ocelots without killing any of them.

The next achievement requires you to defeat the Mooshroom Monstrosity in the '???' secret mission (again, see 'Secret Missions') using only gear unique to the Jungle missions. You may need to grind a little until you have a full set which will allow you to defeat the Mooshroom Monstrosity on the lowest difficulty setting.
NONE - Unequip your ranged weapon, else the achievement won't unlock!
Defeat the Mooshroom Monstrosity using only gear unique to the jungle.
Creeping Winter was released on September 8, 2020, and included five achievements for 120 Gamerscore.

For the first mission, unequip your melee and ranged. After completing the mission without equipping melee or ranged at any time, you will unlock 'Frozen Fists'. You can do this on the lowest difficulty and speed-run the mission with relative ease.
Complete Frosted Fjord without having a melee or ranged weapon equipped at any time.
After completing the 'Lone Fortress' mission on Adventure or Apocalypse difficulty, you will unlock 'Lone Champion'.
Complete Lone Fortress on Adventure or Apocalypse difficulty.
See 'Secret Missions' for information about how to unlock the 'Lost Settlement' secret mission. Complete it on any difficulty to earn 'Lost in the Snow'.
Complete the Lost Settlement secret mission.

Throughout the Creeping Winter missions you'll encounter patches of ice, which you slide on. You should get 'Smooth Operator' naturally, however if you want to get it quickly, find an open patch of ice and run in circles for a couple of minutes.
Slide a total distance of 500 blocks on ice.

The Ice Wand is a new artefact, which can be found in the Frosted Fjord and Lone Fortress missions. Defeat 5 enemies with a single attack of the Ice Want to unlock 'Chill Out'. I would recommend playing through normally until one drops, then going back to camp and restarting a mission on the lowest difficulty to make it easier to defeat enemies. If you're having trouble getting 5 enemies with one hit, the Secret Level '???' is perfect for getting large groups of enemies huddled together.
Defeat 5 mobs with a single Ice Wand attack
